decision.expected_measurable_effect: Expected recordable effects of the complete experiment versus the baseline record, stated separately and without causal attribution. Terminal reach: expected approximately unchanged; if the added tip-speed cost trades away position authority, terminal_error_m could drift upward toward the recorded 0.01 m reach tolerance, so reach_passed = true should be re-checked as an acceptance guard. Sampled holding position: ambiguous directionally; the same six-sample final-window statistics (error_m range 0.007642608585867386-0.05813810428573256 m in the baseline) may contract if residual motion was driving position wander, or may widen if relative down-weighting of tracking increases drift. Sampled holding speed: this is the primary target - expect holding-window speed_m_s range and terminal_speed_m_s to move below the baseline 0.6351726092425104-1.5810152739742807 m/s band; full attainment of the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit within one complete run is not expected, so a reportable partial reduction is a useful outcome. Computation: expected neutral-to-slightly-worse; adding nonzero quadratic tip-speed terms can add solver work, and with mean_update_s 17.26331904856488 s against control_period_s 0.01 s, deadline_misses 35 of 35 update_count and stopping_counts User_Requested_Stop 34 / Solve_Succeeded 1, the run may still stop on budget rather than tolerance, so no solve-time improvement is predicted. Possible adverse effects to watch: terminal_error_m regressing past reach_tolerance_m; larger cost magnitude worsening solver conditioning, iteration count or deadline misses; and the holding term contributing nothing on plans whose effective horizon does not reach the configured settling-window start, which would leave the enlarged holding cost inert and make a null speed result uninformative. Observations that would weaken the hypothesis: a complete run whose holding-window and terminal speeds stay in the baseline band while deadline misses or solve times rise; a pattern of budget-limited stops (budget_best_feasible-type) with no speed or position change; a terminal reach regression with no speed benefit; or any future local screening at a saved update showing no change in projected terminal/holding speed at the changed weight.
decision.rationale: Bounded experiment on the accepted diagnosis: the retained baseline (execution cf997605885642759ee33920e2c9e2ef, controller.gvs_nmpc 7.0.0, parameters 1.0.0, numerical_source bundled_guess) records reach_passed = true with terminal_error_m 0.007642608585867386 m inside reach_tolerance_m 0.01 m, but holding_speed_passed = false over the six recorded final-window samples (speed_m_s 0.6351726092425104 to 1.5810152739742807 m/s, terminal_speed_m_s 0.6351726092425104 m/s) and holding_position_passed = false over the same window, against settling_criteria speed_limit_m_s 0.02 m/s and position_limit_m 0.01 m. The recipe records terminal_tip_speed_weight = 0.0 and holding_tip_speed_weight = 0.0 with tip_speed_scale_m_s = 0.02 m/s, i.e. both tip-speed penalties are currently disabled, which is the testable candidate identified in the diagnosis (status "possible"; raw weight magnitudes do not establish relative cost-term importance and no causality is claimed). Hypothesis to test: a small positive penalty on squared tip speed will add a cost incentive against residual holding-window motion that the position/velocity terms alone did not remove. I select both weights positive because the failure evidence is split between window motion across the whole window (holding term, whose support is the nodes at/after the settling-window start) and the final-node speed (terminal term, a single scaled squared-speed term); the holding value is set larger (0.05 vs 0.01) because its support covers the failing window rather than one node. Values are deliberately small relative to tip_speed_scale_m_s = 0.02 m/s, so that with observed ~0.6-1.6 m/s speeds the added term is material but not dominant over tracking_weight 1.0 and terminal_weight 5.0. Structure is preserved exactly as instructed: terminal speed cost stays a single terminal scaled squared-speed term, holding speed cost stays an integration-step-weighted sum at the scheduled holding nodes, and both the scaling (tip_speed_scale_m_s) and the node scheduling (settling window_s = 0.05 s) are unchanged. No local_comparison is requested: this phase has no evidence read allowance, displayed per-update effective_horizon values for the retained records are 2, 4, 6, 7 and 10 control intervals, and no saved baseline update whose effective plan horizon is 0.01 s is displayed, so a legal saved state cannot be identified from what I may consult; the grant states unavailable/inconclusive screening does not prohibit the complete experiment, so the single complete changed candidate is requested instead.
